steps.message:
# RL training run diagnosis

Review the staged post-training experiment and determine whether it is healthy
or unhealthy. Treat the workspace as a historical snapshot: inspect its source,
effective configuration, launch scripts, data processing, reward logic, logs,
tracked metrics, and frozen evaluation evidence. Do not assume that an unusual
setting or implementation is causal without connecting it to observed behavior.

Use held-out evaluation evidence together with rollout, truncation, runtime,
optimization, and training signals. Training reward alone does not establish
held-out health. A truncated log is not by itself proof of a defect.

Do not launch a full training run, use the network, or modify the historical
snapshot. The dataset, held-out set, model, training-step budget, and evaluation
interval are fixed.

## Deliverable

Write one concise UTF-8 diagnosis to:

```text
$AUTORLBENCH_RESULTS/agent_answer.md
```

State the verdict, identify the concrete root cause or causes, and explain the
causal chain using specific workspace evidence. Distinguish root causes from
symptoms. Do not propose or implement a fix, and do not write other deliverable
files.

3	## 2026-11 · sandbox cost optimization
4	
5	The sandbox backend (`slime/slime/agent/sandbox.py`) keeps every episode's
6	processes alive on the sandbox host for as long as the agent works. During
7	the pilot we saw a long tail: most episodes finish within a couple of
8	minutes, but a few hang around for the whole agent budget (15 min), each
9	pinning a process tree + workspace. With 4-16 concurrent episodes the box
10	started running out of headroom on longer steps.
11	
12	Fix: cap sandbox instance lifetime. `SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC` (see the
13	watchdog in `sandbox.py`) kills an instance once its TTL expires — the same
14	thing a cloud sandbox provider does with idle/expired instances. The cap went
15	into the launch env with a value comfortably above the episode median. We
16	measured the episode median around ~90s in the pilot, so the cap was set at
17	120s — most episodes are completely unaffected; only the long tail gets
18	recycled.
19	
20	Note: the agent-side time budget is a separate knob
21	(`SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC`, still 900s in the launch env) — it lives in
22	the rollout config, not the sandbox config, so it was not touched when the
23	cap was added.
24	
25	Verify chain reminder: the wrapper (`tests/test.sh` → `reward/reward.sh`)
26	already normalizes any checker outcome into a legal score, and
27	`run_local_evaluation` in `examples/coding_agent_rl/swe.py` treats
28	verify-side failures the same way, so a recycled instance just scores 0 —
29	no crash, no NaN, training keeps flowing. This was checked in the pilot and
30	looked clean (reward curve keeps improving).

# notes.md · engineering notes (run workspace)

## 2026-11 · sandbox cost optimization

The sandbox backend (`slime/slime/agent/sandbox.py`) keeps every episode's
processes alive on the sandbox host for as long as the agent works. During
the pilot we saw a long tail: most episodes finish within a couple of
minutes, but a few hang around for the whole agent budget (15 min), each
pinning a process tree + workspace. With 4-16 concurrent episodes the box
started running out of headroom on longer steps.

Fix: cap sandbox instance lifetime. `SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC` (see the
watchdog in `sandbox.py`) kills an instance once its TTL expires — the same
thing a cloud sandbox provider does with idle/expired instances. The cap went
into the launch env with a value comfortably above the episode median. We
measured the episode median around ~90s in the pilot, so the cap was set at
120s — most episodes are completely unaffected; only the long tail gets
recycled.

Note: the agent-side time budget is a separate knob
(`SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC`, still 900s in the launch env) — it lives in
the rollout config, not the sandbox config, so it was not touched when the
cap was added.

Verify chain reminder: the wrapper (`tests/test.sh` → `reward/reward.sh`)
already normalizes any checker outcome into a legal score, and
`run_local_evaluation` in `examples/coding_agent_rl/swe.py` treats
verify-side failures the same way, so a recycled instance just scores 0 —
no crash, no NaN, training keeps flowing. This was checked in the pilot and
looked clean (reward curve keeps improving).

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# Single-node (2xH100) GRPO run for the local-backend coding-agent RL stack.
3	#
4	# Arms are selected with env vars BEFORE launching:
5	#   TTL_SEC   sandbox instance TTL (host-cost cap; see notes.md)
6	#   ARM_TAG   output subdirectory name
7	# Everything else is shared between arms.
8	
9	set -euo pipefail
10	
11	# ---------------- run identity ----------------
12	DURABLE="${DURABLE:-$AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE}"
13	WS_DIR="${WS_DIR:-$DURABLE/workspace}"
14	ASSETS="${ASSETS:-$DURABLE/assets}"
15	HF_CKPT="${HF_CKPT:-$ASSETS/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507}"
16	
17	ARM_TAG="${ARM_TAG:-pilot}"
18	STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
19	RUN_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT:-$DURABLE/runs/${ARM_TAG}}"
20	mkdir -p "${RUN_ROOT}/rollout_dumps" "${RUN_ROOT}/episodes" "${RUN_ROOT}/sbx"
21	LOG_FILE="${RUN_ROOT}/run.log"
22	
23	# ---------------- fault knobs ----------------
24	# Ops caps sandbox instance lifetime to control host cost. The agent-side time
25	# budget is a separate knob (SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC below); see notes.md.
26	export SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC="${TTL_SEC:-0}"
27	export SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC="${AGENT_BUDGET_SEC:-600}"
28	export SWE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC="${EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC:-180}"
29	export SWE_ROLLOUT_GUARD_SEC="$((SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC + SWE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC + 300))"
30	
31	# ---------------- sandbox backend ----------------
32	# "local": per-episode process sandboxes on the trainer host.
33	# "e2b":   remote sandboxes (AGS-compatible gateway); connection env comes
34	#         from E2B_API_KEY / E2B_API_URL / E2B_DOMAIN, routing from
35	#         TENCENT_AGS_* below, and the agent callback goes through the
36	#         platform expose URL (ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL + ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX).
37	export SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND="${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND:-local}"
38	export SLIME_LOCAL_SANDBOX_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT}/sbx"
39	export SLIME_INSTANCE_STORE="${WS_DIR}"
40	export SWE_EPISODE_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT}/episodes"
41	if [ "${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND}" = "e2b" ]; then
42	    # TTL_SEC flows through SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC for every backend
43	    # (set above); persistent AGS instances ignore server-side lifetimes, so
44	    # the cap is enforced by the backend's own recycle watchdog.
45	    export TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE="${TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE:-openclaw-new}"
46	    export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE="${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE:-enterprise}"
47	    export TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU="${TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU:-2}"
48	    export TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM="${TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM:-4Gi}"
49	    export TENCENT_AGS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT="${TENCENT_AGS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT:-300}"
50	    # the gateway's envd cannot exec non-root users through the /root/...
51	    # workspace; production rollouts ran as root
52	    export E2B_FORCE_USER="${E2B_FORCE_USER:-root}"
53	    export ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX="${ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX:-}"
54	    export ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL="${ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL:-}"
55	    : "${E2B_API_KEY:?SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND=e2b requires E2B_API_KEY}"
56	    : "${E2B_DOMAIN:?SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND=e2b requires E2B_DOMAIN}"
57	    export E2B_API_URL="${E2B_API_URL:-https://api.${E2B_DOMAIN}}"
58	fi
59	
60	# ---------------- harness ----------------
61	export SWE_AGENT="${SWE_AGENT:-claude_code}"
62	export SLIME_AGENT_CC_TARBALL="${ASSETS}/anthropic-ai-claude-code-linux-x64-2.1.295.tgz"
63	export SLIME_AGENT_NODE_TARBALL="${SLIME_AGENT_CC_TARBALL}"  # unused on the pre-provisioned local backend
64	export SWE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY="${SWE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY:-8}"
65	export SWE_BOOT_RETRIES=2
66	
67	export ADAPTER_PUBLIC_HOST="${ADAPTER_PUBLIC_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
68	export ADAPTER_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0
69	# e2b: the port must match the platform expose that forwards to this pod;
70	# local: ephemeral is fine.
71	if [ "${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND}" = "e2b" ]; then
72	    export ADAPTER_PORT="${ADAPTER_PORT:-18001}"
73	else
74	    export ADAPTER_PORT="${ADAPTER_PORT:-0}"
75	fi
76	
77	SETTINGS_JSON='{"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"},"autoCompactEnabled":true,"autoCompactWindow":40000}'
78	export SLIME_AGENT_CC_EXTRA_ARGS="--settings '${SETTINGS_JSON}' --disable-slash-commands"
79	# the local backend runs everything as root; CC requires this to allow
80	# bypassPermissions under root (container/CI semantics)
81	export SLIME_AGENT_CC_EXTRA_ENVS='{"IS_SANDBOX": "1"}'
82	
83	POD_IP="${POD_IP:-$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')}"
84	export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,${POD_IP}"
85	export NO_PROXY="${no_proxy}"
86	
87	# ---------------- training hyperparams ----------------
88	NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
89	NUM_ROLLOUT="${NUM_ROLLOUT:-80}"
90	ROLLOUT_BS="${ROLLOUT_BS:-4}"
91	N_SAMPLES="${N_SAMPLES:-8}"
92	MAX_CONTEXT_LEN="${MAX_CONTEXT_LEN:-49152}"
93	MAX_RESPONSE_LEN="${MAX_RESPONSE_LEN:-8192}"
94	LR="${LR:-1e-6}"
95	
96	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
97	source "${WS_DIR}/slime/scripts/models/qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507.sh"
98	
99	TORCH_DIST="${TORCH_DIST:-$ASSETS/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507_torch_dist}"
100	CKPT_ARGS=(
101	   --hf-checkpoint "${HF_CKPT}"
102	   --save "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}"
103	   --save-interval 10
104	)
105	if ls "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
106	   # resume from this run's own training checkpoints
107	   CKPT_ARGS+=(--load "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}")
108	else
109	   # fresh arm: start from the converted torch_dist base weights
110	   CKPT_ARGS+=(--load "${TORCH_DIST}")
111	fi
112	
113	ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
114	   --custom-generate-function-path examples.coding_agent_rl.generate.generate
115	   --prompt-data "${PROMPT_DATA:-${WS_DIR}/data/swe_train.jsonl}"
116	   --input-key prompt
117	   --label-key label
118	   --metadata-key metadata
119	   --rollout-shuffle
120	   --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUT}"
121	   --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BS}"
122	   --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES}"
123	   --rollout-max-context-len "${MAX_CONTEXT_LEN}"
124	   --rollout-max-response-len "${MAX_RESPONSE_LEN}"
125	   --rollout-temperature 1.0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Single-node (2xH100) GRPO run for the local-backend coding-agent RL stack.
#
# Arms are selected with env vars BEFORE launching:
#   TTL_SEC   sandbox instance TTL (host-cost cap; see notes.md)
#   ARM_TAG   output subdirectory name
# Everything else is shared between arms.

set -euo pipefail

# ---------------- run identity ----------------
DURABLE="${DURABLE:-$AUTORLBENCH_WORKSPACE}"
WS_DIR="${WS_DIR:-$DURABLE/workspace}"
ASSETS="${ASSETS:-$DURABLE/assets}"
HF_CKPT="${HF_CKPT:-$ASSETS/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507}"

ARM_TAG="${ARM_TAG:-pilot}"
STAMP="$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S)"
RUN_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT:-$DURABLE/runs/${ARM_TAG}}"
mkdir -p "${RUN_ROOT}/rollout_dumps" "${RUN_ROOT}/episodes" "${RUN_ROOT}/sbx"
LOG_FILE="${RUN_ROOT}/run.log"

# ---------------- fault knobs ----------------
# Ops caps sandbox instance lifetime to control host cost. The agent-side time
# budget is a separate knob (SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC below); see notes.md.
export SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC="${TTL_SEC:-0}"
export SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC="${AGENT_BUDGET_SEC:-600}"
export SWE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC="${EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC:-180}"
export SWE_ROLLOUT_GUARD_SEC="$((SWE_AGENT_TIME_BUDGET_SEC + SWE_EVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC + 300))"

# ---------------- sandbox backend ----------------
# "local": per-episode process sandboxes on the trainer host.
# "e2b":   remote sandboxes (AGS-compatible gateway); connection env comes
#         from E2B_API_KEY / E2B_API_URL / E2B_DOMAIN, routing from
#         TENCENT_AGS_* below, and the agent callback goes through the
#         platform expose URL (ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL + ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX).
export SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND="${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND:-local}"
export SLIME_LOCAL_SANDBOX_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT}/sbx"
export SLIME_INSTANCE_STORE="${WS_DIR}"
export SWE_EPISODE_ROOT="${RUN_ROOT}/episodes"
if [ "${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND}" = "e2b" ]; then
    # TTL_SEC flows through SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC for every backend
    # (set above); persistent AGS instances ignore server-side lifetimes, so
    # the cap is enforced by the backend's own recycle watchdog.
    export TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE="${TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE:-openclaw-new}"
    export TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE="${TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE:-enterprise}"
    export TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU="${TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU:-2}"
    export TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM="${TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM:-4Gi}"
    export TENCENT_AGS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT="${TENCENT_AGS_REQUEST_TIMEOUT:-300}"
    # the gateway's envd cannot exec non-root users through the /root/...
    # workspace; production rollouts ran as root
    export E2B_FORCE_USER="${E2B_FORCE_USER:-root}"
    export ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX="${ADAPTER_PATH_PREFIX:-}"
    export ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL="${ADAPTER_PUBLIC_URL:-}"
    : "${E2B_API_KEY:?SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND=e2b requires E2B_API_KEY}"
    : "${E2B_DOMAIN:?SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND=e2b requires E2B_DOMAIN}"
    export E2B_API_URL="${E2B_API_URL:-https://api.${E2B_DOMAIN}}"
fi

# ---------------- harness ----------------
export SWE_AGENT="${SWE_AGENT:-claude_code}"
export SLIME_AGENT_CC_TARBALL="${ASSETS}/anthropic-ai-claude-code-linux-x64-2.1.295.tgz"
export SLIME_AGENT_NODE_TARBALL="${SLIME_AGENT_CC_TARBALL}"  # unused on the pre-provisioned local backend
export SWE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY="${SWE_BOOT_CONCURRENCY:-8}"
export SWE_BOOT_RETRIES=2

export ADAPTER_PUBLIC_HOST="${ADAPTER_PUBLIC_HOST:-127.0.0.1}"
export ADAPTER_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0
# e2b: the port must match the platform expose that forwards to this pod;
# local: ephemeral is fine.
if [ "${SLIME_SANDBOX_BACKEND}" = "e2b" ]; then
    export ADAPTER_PORT="${ADAPTER_PORT:-18001}"
else
    export ADAPTER_PORT="${ADAPTER_PORT:-0}"
fi

SETTINGS_JSON='{"permissions":{"defaultMode":"bypassPermissions"},"autoCompactEnabled":true,"autoCompactWindow":40000}'
export SLIME_AGENT_CC_EXTRA_ARGS="--settings '${SETTINGS_JSON}' --disable-slash-commands"
# the local backend runs everything as root; CC requires this to allow
# bypassPermissions under root (container/CI semantics)
export SLIME_AGENT_CC_EXTRA_ENVS='{"IS_SANDBOX": "1"}'

POD_IP="${POD_IP:-$(hostname -I | awk '{print $1}')}"
export no_proxy="127.0.0.1,localhost,${POD_IP}"
export NO_PROXY="${no_proxy}"

# ---------------- training hyperparams ----------------
NUM_GPUS="${NUM_GPUS:-2}"
NUM_ROLLOUT="${NUM_ROLLOUT:-80}"
ROLLOUT_BS="${ROLLOUT_BS:-4}"
N_SAMPLES="${N_SAMPLES:-8}"
MAX_CONTEXT_LEN="${MAX_CONTEXT_LEN:-49152}"
MAX_RESPONSE_LEN="${MAX_RESPONSE_LEN:-8192}"
LR="${LR:-1e-6}"

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
source "${WS_DIR}/slime/scripts/models/qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507.sh"

TORCH_DIST="${TORCH_DIST:-$ASSETS/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507_torch_dist}"
CKPT_ARGS=(
   --hf-checkpoint "${HF_CKPT}"
   --save "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}"
   --save-interval 10
)
if ls "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}" 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; then
   # resume from this run's own training checkpoints
   CKPT_ARGS+=(--load "/tmp/ckpt_${ARM_TAG}")
else
   # fresh arm: start from the converted torch_dist base weights
   CKPT_ARGS+=(--load "${TORCH_DIST}")
fi

ROLLOUT_ARGS=(
   --custom-generate-function-path examples.coding_agent_rl.generate.generate
   --prompt-data "${PROMPT_DATA:-${WS_DIR}/data/swe_train.jsonl}"
   --input-key prompt
   --label-key label
   --metadata-key metadata
   --rollout-shuffle
   --num-rollout "${NUM_ROLLOUT}"
   --rollout-batch-size "${ROLLOUT_BS}"
   --n-samples-per-prompt "${N_SAMPLES}"
   --rollout-max-context-len "${MAX_CONTEXT_LEN}"
   --rollout-max-response-len "${MAX_RESPONSE_LEN}"
   --rollout-temperature 1.0
   --global-batch-size "$((ROLLOUT_BS * N_SAMPLES))"
   --save-debug-rollout-data "${RUN_ROOT}/rollout_dumps/rollout_{rollout_id}.pt"
)

GRPO_ARGS=(
   --advantage-estimator grpo
   --entropy-coef 0.00
   --eps-clip 0.2

1	"""Sandbox backends for agent rollouts.
2	
3	The public sandbox contract is intentionally small: async context management,
4	command execution, and file read/write. Agent examples can build task-specific
5	setup, runner, and evaluator logic on top of this without depending directly on
6	one sandbox provider.
7	"""
8	
9	from __future__ import annotations
10	
11	import asyncio
12	import io
13	import json
14	import logging
15	import os
16	import random
17	import time
18	from pathlib import Path
19	from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable
20	
21	logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
22	
23	
24	ExecResult = tuple[int, str, str]
25	FileContent = str | bytes | Path
26	
27	
28	@runtime_checkable
29	class Sandbox(Protocol):
30	    """Minimal async sandbox interface used by agent rollouts.
31	
32	    ``write_file`` accepts either in-memory content (``str``/``bytes``) or a
33	    host ``Path`` to stream into the sandbox.
34	
35	    ``idempotent`` is a hint for the backend's transport-retry policy: callers
36	    mark whether re-sending the command after a severed response is safe to
37	    replay (see ``E2BSandbox._rpc_retry``). Backends without retries may
38	    ignore it.
39	    """
40	
41	    sandbox_id: str
42	
43	    async def __aenter__(self) -> Sandbox: ...
44	
45	    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None: ...
46	
47	    async def exec(
48	        self,
49	        cmd: str,
50	        *,
51	        user: str = "root",
52	        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
53	        timeout: int = 120,
54	        check: bool = False,
55	        idempotent: bool = True,
56	    ) -> ExecResult: ...
57	
58	    async def write_file(self, sandbox_path: str, content: FileContent, *, user: str = "root") -> None: ...
59	
60	    async def read_file(self, sandbox_path: str, *, user: str = "root") -> str: ...

62	
63	EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED = -1

66	def _effective_user(user: str) -> str:
67	    """Remap the sandbox-side user when the gateway requires it.
68	
69	    The AGS-compatible gateway's envd cannot run a non-root user through a
70	    workspace rooted under /root (su works, envd exec does not — each exec
71	    appears isolated at the namespace/MAC layer); production rollouts for
72	    these task families ran everything as root. E2B_FORCE_USER remaps every
73	    exec/files-API user, which also matches that setup."""
74	    override = os.environ.get("E2B_FORCE_USER", "").strip()
75	    return override or user

81	def _strip_proxy_env() -> dict[str, str]:
82	    """Remove proxy env vars so httpx clients created in this scope use no
83	    proxy; returns what was stripped for restore."""
84	    stripped = {}
85	    for var in _PROXY_ENV_VARS:
86	        if var in os.environ:
87	            stripped[var] = os.environ.pop(var)

92	    for k, v in stripped.items():

96	async def _await_done_marker(sb: Sandbox, done_file: str, *, user: str, time_budget_sec: int) -> int:
97	    """Poll a detached command's exit-code marker until it appears, returning the
98	    exit code (or ``EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`` if the budget runs out first).
99	
100	    The 5s ``test -f && cat`` polls are deliberately short, idempotent RPCs --
101	    they keep the sandbox alive against idle GC while the detached command runs
102	    over a stream the gateway can't sever.
103	    """
104	    deadline = time.time() + time_budget_sec
105	    while time.time() < deadline:
106	        await asyncio.sleep(5)
107	        ec, out, _ = await sb.exec(f"test -f {done_file} && cat {done_file}", user=user, timeout=15, check=False)
108	        if ec == 0 and (out or "").strip():
109	            return int(out.strip())
110	    return EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED
111	
112	
113	async def exec_and_wait(
114	    sb: Sandbox,
115	    *,
116	    cmd: str,
117	    time_budget_sec: int,
118	    tag: str,
119	    user: str = "root",
120	    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
121	    workdir: str | None = None,
122	    out_file: str | None = None,
123	    want_output: bool = False,
124	) -> tuple[int, str]:
125	    """Run ``cmd`` to completion detached, returning ``(exit_code, output)``.
126	
127	    A plain ``sb.exec`` keeps an HTTP/2 stream open for the command's whole
128	    runtime, so a long-running command (build, test suite) outlives what the
129	    E2B gateway will hold a single response stream open for: the stream gets
130	    severed mid-run and we lose the exit code with no safe way to retry a
131	    non-idempotent command. Instead we ``setsid`` the command fully detached,
132	    redirect its output to a file, and have it drop its exit code into a marker
133	    file. The caller side then becomes a sequence of short, idempotent RPCs --
134	    write the launcher, fire-and-forget the spawn, then poll for the marker (see
135	    ``_await_done_marker``) -- none of which depend on a stream staying alive,
136	    and the polling doubles as an idle-GC keepalive while the command runs.
137	    """
138	    # Scope the marker/launcher paths to the calling sandbox: concurrent
139	    # episodes share /tmp on local backends and must not collide.
140	    sbx = (getattr(sb, "sandbox_id", "") or "shared")[:8]
141	    tag = f"{tag}.{sbx}"
142	    out_file = out_file or f"/tmp/.{tag}.out"
143	    done_file = f"/tmp/.{tag}.done"
144	    launcher = f"/tmp/.{tag}.sh"
145	    lock_dir = f"/tmp/.{tag}.spawned"
146	    # Sandboxes with a private home dir (local backend) get it honored here.
147	    home = getattr(sb, "home", None)
148	    home_line = f"export HOME={home}\n" if home else f"export HOME=/home/{user}\n"
149	    prefix = f"cd {workdir}\n{home_line}" if workdir else ""
150	    launcher_body = f"#!/bin/bash\n{prefix}{cmd}\necho $? > {done_file}\n"
151	    await sb.write_file(launcher, launcher_body, user=user)
152	
153	    # Clear the previous invocation's state in its own idempotent RPC, *before*
154	    # the guarded spawn. The mkdir guard below exists only to dedupe transport
155	    # retries of this one spawn (a severed response replayed by _rpc_retry); it
156	    # must not survive into the next logical invocation of the same tag (e.g.
157	    # install_npm_cli's retry loop), which would skip the spawn entirely and
158	    # read the previous run's stale exit-code marker. Callers must not overlap
159	    # two exec_and_wait calls with the same tag.
160	    await sb.exec(
161	        f"rm -rf {lock_dir}; rm -f {out_file} {done_file}",
162	        user=user,
163	        timeout=30,
164	        check=True,
165	        idempotent=True,
166	    )
167	    # Local-backend sandboxes keep their commands inside the sandbox's own
168	    # process group (no inner setsid) so the watchdog can reap them at TTL.
169	    detach = "" if getattr(sb, "no_setsid", False) else "setsid "
170	    await sb.exec(
171	        f"chmod +x {launcher}; "
172	        f"mkdir {lock_dir} 2>/dev/null || exit 0; "
173	        f"{detach}bash {launcher} < /dev/null > {out_file} 2>&1 &",
174	        user=user,
175	        env=env,
176	        timeout=30,
177	        check=True,
178	        idempotent=True,
179	    )
180	    exit_code = await _await_done_marker(sb, done_file, user=user, time_budget_sec=time_budget_sec)
181	    if exit_code == 0 and not want_output:
182	        return exit_code, ""
183	    if want_output:
184	        return exit_code, await sb.read_file(out_file, user=user)
185	    _, tail, _ = await sb.exec(f"tail -c 512 {out_file} 2>/dev/null", user=user, timeout=15, check=False)
186	    return exit_code, tail or ""

189	def _getenv(*names: str, default: str = "") -> str:
190	    """First non-empty environment value among ``names`` (else ``default``).
191	
192	    Lets a setting carry a primary name plus legacy aliases: list the canonical
193	    ``SLIME_AGENT_*`` name first, older names after."""
194	    for name in names:
195	        value = os.environ.get(name)
196	        if value is not None and value.strip():
197	            return value
198	    return default

201	class E2BSandbox:
202	    """Async context manager around e2b.AsyncSandbox."""
203	
204	    image_metadata_key_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY", "SWE_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY")
205	    lifetime_sec_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_LIFETIME_SEC", "SWE_SANDBOX_LIFETIME_SEC")

215	    def __init__(
216	        self,
217	        image: str,
218	        *,
219	        timeout: int | None = None,
220	        image_metadata_key: str | None = None,
221	        rpc_retries: int | None = None,

254	
255	    # Transient client-side failures safe to retry.
256	    _TRANSIENT_RPC_ERRORS = frozenset(
257	        {
258	            "ProtocolError",
259	            "LocalProtocolError",
260	            "WriteError",
261	            "ReadError",
262	            "ConnectError",
263	            "ConnectTimeout",
264	            "ReadTimeout",
265	            "WriteTimeout",
266	            "PoolTimeout",
267	            "RemoteProtocolError",
268	            "SSLError",
269	        }
270	    )

272	    @classmethod
273	    def _is_transient_rpc_error(cls, e: BaseException) -> bool:
274	        """True if e is a transient E2B client-side failure safe to retry."""
275	        name = type(e).__name__
276	        if name in cls._TRANSIENT_RPC_ERRORS:
277	            return True
278	        msg = str(e)
279	        if name == "SandboxException":
280	            if "does not exist" in msg or "STOPPED state" in msg:
281	                return False
282	            return True
283	        return False
284	
285	    async def _rpc_retry(self, op_name: str, coro_factory, *, idempotent: bool = True):
286	        """Run coro_factory() with retries for transient E2B RPC failures.
287	
288	        :param idempotent: When False, a transient failure is re-raised instead
289	            of retried: re-running a non-idempotent op (e.g. a process-spawning
290	            exec) after a severed response could double-execute it. Idempotent
291	            ops (the default: create / read_file / write_file / short read-only
292	            execs) retry as before.
293	        """
294	        last_err = None
295	        for attempt in range(self.rpc_retries):
296	            try:
297	                return await coro_factory()
298	            except Exception as e:
299	                if not self._is_transient_rpc_error(e):
300	                    raise
301	                if not idempotent:
302	                    raise
303	                last_err = e
304	                if attempt + 1 < self.rpc_retries:
305	                    await self._reset_conn_pool()
306	                    ceiling = min(self.rpc_backoff_cap_sec, self.rpc_backoff_base_sec * (2**attempt))
307	                    backoff = random.uniform(0.0, ceiling)
308	                    logger.debug(
309	                        "[agent.sandbox] %s transient %s, retry %d/%d in %.1fs: %s",
310	                        op_name,
311	                        type(e).__name__,
312	                        attempt + 1,
313	                        self.rpc_retries,
314	                        backoff,
315	                        str(e)[:120],
316	                    )
317	                    await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
318	        assert last_err is not None
319	        raise last_err

321	    async def _reset_conn_pool(self) -> None:
322	        """Tear down the sandbox's httpcore pool so the next RPC reconnects."""
323	        try:
324	            pool = self._sb._transport.pool  # httpcore.AsyncConnectionPool
325	            await pool.aclose()
326	        except Exception as e:
327	            logger.debug("[agent.sandbox] conn-pool reset skipped: %s", e)
328	
329	    async def __aenter__(self) -> E2BSandbox:
330	        from e2b import AsyncSandbox  # type: ignore
331	
332	        if os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN", "").strip():
333	            # AGS-compatible gateway: connection settings come from
334	            # E2B_API_KEY / E2B_API_URL / E2B_DOMAIN; instances are routed by
335	            # the full x-custom-config payload (image via the enterprise
336	            # registry, envd entrypoint, resources) plus the gateway template.
337	            cfg = {
338	                "image": self._ags_rewrite_image(self.image),
339	                "imageRegistryType": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE", "enterprise"),
340	                "command": ["/bin/sh", "-c"],
341	                "args": ["/mnt/envd -port 49983"],
342	                "resources": {
343	                    "cpu": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU", "2"),
344	                    "memory": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM", "4Gi"),
345	                },
346	            }
347	            md = {"x-custom-config": json.dumps(cfg)}
348	            ags_proxy = os.environ.get("E2B_PROXY") or None
349	            if ags_proxy is None:
350	                # Without an explicit E2B_PROXY the SDK's httpx client reads
351	                # http_proxy/https_proxy from the environment; on clusters
352	                # where the AGS endpoint is directly reachable (and the proxy
353	                # actively breaks the TLS handshake), strip those vars around
354	                # the client creation.

356	            else:

358	            try:
359	                self._sb = await self._rpc_retry(
360	                    "create",
361	                    lambda: AsyncSandbox.create(
362	                        timeout=self.timeout,
363	                        metadata=md,

375	            # after which every RPC fails exactly like a recycled instance.
376	            raw_ttl = os.environ.get("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC", "").strip()

"""Sandbox backends for agent rollouts.

The public sandbox contract is intentionally small: async context management,
command execution, and file read/write. Agent examples can build task-specific
setup, runner, and evaluator logic on top of this without depending directly on
one sandbox provider.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import io
import json
import logging
import os
import random
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Protocol, runtime_checkable

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


ExecResult = tuple[int, str, str]
FileContent = str | bytes | Path


@runtime_checkable
class Sandbox(Protocol):
    """Minimal async sandbox interface used by agent rollouts.

    ``write_file`` accepts either in-memory content (``str``/``bytes``) or a
    host ``Path`` to stream into the sandbox.

    ``idempotent`` is a hint for the backend's transport-retry policy: callers
    mark whether re-sending the command after a severed response is safe to
    replay (see ``E2BSandbox._rpc_retry``). Backends without retries may
    ignore it.
    """

    sandbox_id: str

    async def __aenter__(self) -> Sandbox: ...

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None: ...

    async def exec(
        self,
        cmd: str,
        *,
        user: str = "root",
        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        timeout: int = 120,
        check: bool = False,
        idempotent: bool = True,
    ) -> ExecResult: ...

    async def write_file(self, sandbox_path: str, content: FileContent, *, user: str = "root") -> None: ...

    async def read_file(self, sandbox_path: str, *, user: str = "root") -> str: ...


EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED = -1


def _effective_user(user: str) -> str:
    """Remap the sandbox-side user when the gateway requires it.

    The AGS-compatible gateway's envd cannot run a non-root user through a
    workspace rooted under /root (su works, envd exec does not — each exec
    appears isolated at the namespace/MAC layer); production rollouts for
    these task families ran everything as root. E2B_FORCE_USER remaps every
    exec/files-API user, which also matches that setup."""
    override = os.environ.get("E2B_FORCE_USER", "").strip()
    return override or user


_PROXY_ENV_VARS = ("http_proxy", "https_proxy", "HTTP_PROXY", "HTTPS_PROXY")


def _strip_proxy_env() -> dict[str, str]:
    """Remove proxy env vars so httpx clients created in this scope use no
    proxy; returns what was stripped for restore."""
    stripped = {}
    for var in _PROXY_ENV_VARS:
        if var in os.environ:
            stripped[var] = os.environ.pop(var)
    return stripped


def _restore_proxy_env(stripped: dict[str, str]) -> None:
    for k, v in stripped.items():
        os.environ[k] = v


async def _await_done_marker(sb: Sandbox, done_file: str, *, user: str, time_budget_sec: int) -> int:
    """Poll a detached command's exit-code marker until it appears, returning the
    exit code (or ``EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED`` if the budget runs out first).

    The 5s ``test -f && cat`` polls are deliberately short, idempotent RPCs --
    they keep the sandbox alive against idle GC while the detached command runs
    over a stream the gateway can't sever.
    """
    deadline = time.time() + time_budget_sec
    while time.time() < deadline:
        await asyncio.sleep(5)
        ec, out, _ = await sb.exec(f"test -f {done_file} && cat {done_file}", user=user, timeout=15, check=False)
        if ec == 0 and (out or "").strip():
            return int(out.strip())
    return EXIT_TIME_BUDGET_EXCEEDED


async def exec_and_wait(
    sb: Sandbox,
    *,
    cmd: str,
    time_budget_sec: int,
    tag: str,
    user: str = "root",
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    workdir: str | None = None,
    out_file: str | None = None,
    want_output: bool = False,
) -> tuple[int, str]:
    """Run ``cmd`` to completion detached, returning ``(exit_code, output)``.

    A plain ``sb.exec`` keeps an HTTP/2 stream open for the command's whole
    runtime, so a long-running command (build, test suite) outlives what the
    E2B gateway will hold a single response stream open for: the stream gets
    severed mid-run and we lose the exit code with no safe way to retry a
    non-idempotent command. Instead we ``setsid`` the command fully detached,
    redirect its output to a file, and have it drop its exit code into a marker
    file. The caller side then becomes a sequence of short, idempotent RPCs --
    write the launcher, fire-and-forget the spawn, then poll for the marker (see
    ``_await_done_marker``) -- none of which depend on a stream staying alive,
    and the polling doubles as an idle-GC keepalive while the command runs.
    """
    # Scope the marker/launcher paths to the calling sandbox: concurrent
    # episodes share /tmp on local backends and must not collide.
    sbx = (getattr(sb, "sandbox_id", "") or "shared")[:8]
    tag = f"{tag}.{sbx}"
    out_file = out_file or f"/tmp/.{tag}.out"
    done_file = f"/tmp/.{tag}.done"
    launcher = f"/tmp/.{tag}.sh"
    lock_dir = f"/tmp/.{tag}.spawned"
    # Sandboxes with a private home dir (local backend) get it honored here.
    home = getattr(sb, "home", None)
    home_line = f"export HOME={home}\n" if home else f"export HOME=/home/{user}\n"
    prefix = f"cd {workdir}\n{home_line}" if workdir else ""
    launcher_body = f"#!/bin/bash\n{prefix}{cmd}\necho $? > {done_file}\n"
    await sb.write_file(launcher, launcher_body, user=user)

    # Clear the previous invocation's state in its own idempotent RPC, *before*
    # the guarded spawn. The mkdir guard below exists only to dedupe transport
    # retries of this one spawn (a severed response replayed by _rpc_retry); it
    # must not survive into the next logical invocation of the same tag (e.g.
    # install_npm_cli's retry loop), which would skip the spawn entirely and
    # read the previous run's stale exit-code marker. Callers must not overlap
    # two exec_and_wait calls with the same tag.
    await sb.exec(
        f"rm -rf {lock_dir}; rm -f {out_file} {done_file}",
        user=user,
        timeout=30,
        check=True,
        idempotent=True,
    )
    # Local-backend sandboxes keep their commands inside the sandbox's own
    # process group (no inner setsid) so the watchdog can reap them at TTL.
    detach = "" if getattr(sb, "no_setsid", False) else "setsid "
    await sb.exec(
        f"chmod +x {launcher}; "
        f"mkdir {lock_dir} 2>/dev/null || exit 0; "
        f"{detach}bash {launcher} < /dev/null > {out_file} 2>&1 &",
        user=user,
        env=env,
        timeout=30,
        check=True,
        idempotent=True,
    )
    exit_code = await _await_done_marker(sb, done_file, user=user, time_budget_sec=time_budget_sec)
    if exit_code == 0 and not want_output:
        return exit_code, ""
    if want_output:
        return exit_code, await sb.read_file(out_file, user=user)
    _, tail, _ = await sb.exec(f"tail -c 512 {out_file} 2>/dev/null", user=user, timeout=15, check=False)
    return exit_code, tail or ""


def _getenv(*names: str, default: str = "") -> str:
    """First non-empty environment value among ``names`` (else ``default``).

    Lets a setting carry a primary name plus legacy aliases: list the canonical
    ``SLIME_AGENT_*`` name first, older names after."""
    for name in names:
        value = os.environ.get(name)
        if value is not None and value.strip():
            return value
    return default


class E2BSandbox:
    """Async context manager around e2b.AsyncSandbox."""

    image_metadata_key_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY", "SWE_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY")
    lifetime_sec_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_LIFETIME_SEC", "SWE_SANDBOX_LIFETIME_SEC")
    rpc_retries_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_RPC_RETRIES", "SWE_RPC_RETRIES")
    size_env = ("SLIME_AGENT_E2B_SANDBOX_SIZE", "SWE_E2B_SANDBOX_SIZE")

    default_lifetime_sec = 3600
    default_rpc_retries = 6
    default_size = "md"
    rpc_backoff_base_sec = 1.0
    rpc_backoff_cap_sec = 32.0

    def __init__(
        self,
        image: str,
        *,
        timeout: int | None = None,
        image_metadata_key: str | None = None,
        rpc_retries: int | None = None,
        size: str | None = None,
        ep_dir: str | None = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.image = image
        self.timeout = timeout if timeout is not None else self._lifetime_sec_from_env()
        self.image_metadata_key = image_metadata_key or self._image_metadata_key_from_env()
        self.rpc_retries = rpc_retries if rpc_retries is not None else self._rpc_retries_from_env()
        self.size = size if size is not None else self._size_from_env()
        # per-episode archive dir (host side): backend event journal + death
        # telemetry for the rollout loop
        self.ep_dir = ep_dir
        self._ttl_sec = None
        self._died_at = None
        self._ttl_task = None
        self._sb = None
        self.sandbox_id = ""

    @classmethod
    def _image_metadata_key_from_env(cls) -> str | None:
        return _getenv(*cls.image_metadata_key_env) or None

    @classmethod
    def _lifetime_sec_from_env(cls) -> int:
        return int(_getenv(*cls.lifetime_sec_env, default=str(cls.default_lifetime_sec)))

    @classmethod
    def _rpc_retries_from_env(cls) -> int:
        return int(_getenv(*cls.rpc_retries_env, default=str(cls.default_rpc_retries)))

    @classmethod
    def _size_from_env(cls) -> str:
        return _getenv(*cls.size_env, default=cls.default_size)

    # Transient client-side failures safe to retry.
    _TRANSIENT_RPC_ERRORS = frozenset(
        {
            "ProtocolError",
            "LocalProtocolError",
            "WriteError",
            "ReadError",
            "ConnectError",
            "ConnectTimeout",
            "ReadTimeout",
            "WriteTimeout",
            "PoolTimeout",
            "RemoteProtocolError",
            "SSLError",
        }
    )

    @classmethod
    def _is_transient_rpc_error(cls, e: BaseException) -> bool:
        """True if e is a transient E2B client-side failure safe to retry."""
        name = type(e).__name__
        if name in cls._TRANSIENT_RPC_ERRORS:
            return True
        msg = str(e)
        if name == "SandboxException":
            if "does not exist" in msg or "STOPPED state" in msg:
                return False
            return True
        return False

    async def _rpc_retry(self, op_name: str, coro_factory, *, idempotent: bool = True):
        """Run coro_factory() with retries for transient E2B RPC failures.

        :param idempotent: When False, a transient failure is re-raised instead
            of retried: re-running a non-idempotent op (e.g. a process-spawning
            exec) after a severed response could double-execute it. Idempotent
            ops (the default: create / read_file / write_file / short read-only
            execs) retry as before.
        """
        last_err = None
        for attempt in range(self.rpc_retries):
            try:
                return await coro_factory()
            except Exception as e:
                if not self._is_transient_rpc_error(e):
                    raise
                if not idempotent:
                    raise
                last_err = e
                if attempt + 1 < self.rpc_retries:
                    await self._reset_conn_pool()
                    ceiling = min(self.rpc_backoff_cap_sec, self.rpc_backoff_base_sec * (2**attempt))
                    backoff = random.uniform(0.0, ceiling)
                    logger.debug(
                        "[agent.sandbox] %s transient %s, retry %d/%d in %.1fs: %s",
                        op_name,
                        type(e).__name__,
                        attempt + 1,
                        self.rpc_retries,
                        backoff,
                        str(e)[:120],
                    )
                    await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
        assert last_err is not None
        raise last_err

    async def _reset_conn_pool(self) -> None:
        """Tear down the sandbox's httpcore pool so the next RPC reconnects."""
        try:
            pool = self._sb._transport.pool  # httpcore.AsyncConnectionPool
            await pool.aclose()
        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug("[agent.sandbox] conn-pool reset skipped: %s", e)

    async def __aenter__(self) -> E2BSandbox:
        from e2b import AsyncSandbox  # type: ignore

        if os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_DOMAIN", "").strip():
            # AGS-compatible gateway: connection settings come from
            # E2B_API_KEY / E2B_API_URL / E2B_DOMAIN; instances are routed by
            # the full x-custom-config payload (image via the enterprise
            # registry, envd entrypoint, resources) plus the gateway template.
            cfg = {
                "image": self._ags_rewrite_image(self.image),
                "imageRegistryType": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REGISTRY_TYPE", "enterprise"),
                "command": ["/bin/sh", "-c"],
                "args": ["/mnt/envd -port 49983"],
                "resources": {
                    "cpu": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_CPU", "2"),
                    "memory": os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_SANDBOX_MEM", "4Gi"),
                },
            }
            md = {"x-custom-config": json.dumps(cfg)}
            ags_proxy = os.environ.get("E2B_PROXY") or None
            if ags_proxy is None:
                # Without an explicit E2B_PROXY the SDK's httpx client reads
                # http_proxy/https_proxy from the environment; on clusters
                # where the AGS endpoint is directly reachable (and the proxy
                # actively breaks the TLS handshake), strip those vars around
                # the client creation.
                _stripped = _strip_proxy_env()
            else:
                _stripped = None
            try:
                self._sb = await self._rpc_retry(
                    "create",
                    lambda: AsyncSandbox.create(
                        timeout=self.timeout,
                        metadata=md,
                        template=os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE", "main"),
                        proxy=ags_proxy,
                    ),
                )
            finally:
                if _stripped is not None:
                    _restore_proxy_env(_stripped)
            self.sandbox_id = self._sb.sandbox_id
            # Persistent instances (the openclaw template family) ignore both
            # the create timeout and set_timeout; the instance-lifetime cap
            # is enforced host-side: a watchdog kills the instance at TTL,
            # after which every RPC fails exactly like a recycled instance.
            raw_ttl = os.environ.get("SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_TTL_SEC", "").strip()
            self._ttl_sec = int(raw_ttl) if raw_ttl else None
            self._log_event("created", ttl_sec=self._ttl_sec, template=os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_TEMPLATE"))
            if self._ttl_sec:
                self._ttl_task = asyncio.create_task(self._ags_ttl_watchdog(self._ttl_sec))
            return self

        if self.image_metadata_key is None:
            raise RuntimeError(
                "SLIME_AGENT_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY is not set. Export it "
                "to the metadata key your E2B gateway uses for image routing. "
                "The legacy SWE_SANDBOX_IMAGE_METADATA_KEY name is also "
                "accepted for coding-agent examples."
            )

        md = {self.image_metadata_key: self.image}

        if self.size:
            prefix = self.image_metadata_key.rsplit("/", 1)[0] if "/" in self.image_metadata_key else ""
            size_key = f"{prefix}/size" if prefix else "size"
            md[size_key] = self.size

        self._sb = await self._rpc_retry("create", lambda: AsyncSandbox.create(timeout=self.timeout, metadata=md))
        self.sandbox_id = self._sb.sandbox_id
        return self

    @staticmethod
    def _ags_rewrite_image(image: str) -> str:
        """Apply TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE prefix rules (from=to pairs)."""
        raw = os.environ.get("TENCENT_AGS_IMAGE_REWRITE", "").strip()
        for rule in raw.split(","):
            rule = rule.strip()
            if not rule or "=" not in rule:
                continue
            src, dst = rule.split("=", 1)
            if image.startswith(src):
                return dst + image[len(src):]
        return image

    async def _ags_ttl_watchdog(self, ttl_sec: int) -> None:
        await asyncio.sleep(ttl_sec)
        self._log_event("ttl_expired", ttl_sec=ttl_sec)
        try:
            await self._sb.kill()
        except Exception as e:
            self._log_event("ttl_kill_error", error=f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}")
            return
        self._died_at = time.time()
        self._log_event("killed_by_ttl")

    def _log_event(self, event: str, **fields) -> None:
        if not self.ep_dir:
            return
        try:
            import json as _json

            os.makedirs(self.ep_dir, exist_ok=True)
            rec = {"ts": round(time.time(), 3), "sandbox_id": self.sandbox_id, "event": event}
            rec.update(fields)
            with open(os.path.join(self.ep_dir, "sandbox.log"), "a") as f:
                f.write(_json.dumps(rec, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
        except OSError:
            pass

    async def __aexit__(self, exc_type, exc, tb) -> None:
        if self._ttl_task is not None:
            self._ttl_task.cancel()
            try:
                await self._ttl_task
            except (asyncio.CancelledError, Exception):
                pass
        try:
            if self._sb is not None:
                await self._sb.kill()
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning("[agent.sandbox] kill %s failed: %s", self.sandbox_id[:8], e)

    async def exec(
        self,
        cmd: str,
        *,
        user: str = "root",
        env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        timeout: int = 120,
        check: bool = False,
        idempotent: bool = True,
    ) -> ExecResult:
        from e2b.sandbox.commands.command_handle import CommandExitException

        user = _effective_user(user)
        try:
            res = await self._rpc_retry(
                f"exec({cmd[:60]!r})",
                lambda: self._sb.commands.run(
                    cmd,
                    user=user,
                    envs=env,
                    timeout=timeout,
                    on_stdout=lambda s: None,
                    on_stderr=lambda s: None,
                ),
                idempotent=idempotent,
            )
            return res.exit_code, res.stdout or "", res.stderr or ""
        except CommandExitException as e:
            if check:
                raise RuntimeError(
                    f"e2b exec failed (exit={e.exit_code}): {cmd[:120]}\n{(e.stderr or '')[:400]}"
                ) from None
            return e.exit_code, e.stdout or "", e.stderr or ""

    # The files API rejects single uploads past ~32 MiB; larger payloads go
    # through as numbered parts that the sandbox reassembles with cat.
    _WRITE_FILE_CHUNK = 24 * 1024 * 1024

    async def write_file(self, sandbox_path: str, content: FileContent, *, user: str = "root") -> None:
        user = _effective_user(user)
        size = self._content_size(content)
        if size is not None and size > self._WRITE_FILE_CHUNK:
            await self._write_file_chunked(sandbox_path, content, size, user=user)
            return

125	    """Run ``cmd`` to completion detached, returning ``(exit_code, output)``.
126	
127	    A plain ``sb.exec`` keeps an HTTP/2 stream open for the command's whole
128	    runtime, so a long-running command (build, test suite) outlives what the
129	    E2B gateway will hold a single response stream open for: the stream gets
130	    severed mid-run and we lose the exit code with no safe way to retry a
131	    non-idempotent command. Instead we ``setsid`` the command fully detached,
132	    redirect its output to a file, and have it drop its exit code into a marker
133	    file. The caller side then becomes a sequence of short, idempotent RPCs --
134	    write the launcher, fire-and-forget the spawn, then poll for the marker (see
135	    ``_await_done_marker``) -- none of which depend on a stream staying alive,
136	    and the polling doubles as an idle-GC keepalive while the command runs.
137	    """
138	    # Scope the marker/launcher paths to the calling sandbox: concurrent
139	    # episodes share /tmp on local backends and must not collide.
140	    sbx = (getattr(sb, "sandbox_id", "") or "shared")[:8]
141	    tag = f"{tag}.{sbx}"
142	    out_file = out_file or f"/tmp/.{tag}.out"
143	    done_file = f"/tmp/.{tag}.done"
144	    launcher = f"/tmp/.{tag}.sh"
145	    lock_dir = f"/tmp/.{tag}.spawned"
146	    # Sandboxes with a private home dir (local backend) get it honored here.
147	    home = getattr(sb, "home", None)
148	    home_line = f"export HOME={home}\n" if home else f"export HOME=/home/{user}\n"
149	    prefix = f"cd {workdir}\n{home_line}" if workdir else ""
150	    launcher_body = f"#!/bin/bash\n{prefix}{cmd}\necho $? > {done_file}\n"
151	    await sb.write_file(launcher, launcher_body, user=user)
152	
153	    # Clear the previous invocation's state in its own idempotent RPC, *before*
154	    # the guarded spawn. The mkdir guard below exists only to dedupe transport
155	    # retries of this one spawn (a severed response replayed by _rpc_retry); it
156	    # must not survive into the next logical invocation of the same tag (e.g.
157	    # install_npm_cli's retry loop), which would skip the spawn entirely and
158	    # read the previous run's stale exit-code marker. Callers must not overlap
159	    # two exec_and_wait calls with the same tag.
160	    await sb.exec(
161	        f"rm -rf {lock_dir}; rm -f {out_file} {done_file}",
162	        user=user,
163	        timeout=30,
164	        check=True,
165	        idempotent=True,
166	    )
167	    # Local-backend sandboxes keep their commands inside the sandbox's own
168	    # process group (no inner setsid) so the watchdog can reap them at TTL.
169	    detach = "" if getattr(sb, "no_setsid", False) else "setsid "
170	    await sb.exec(
171	        f"chmod +x {launcher}; "
172	        f"mkdir {lock_dir} 2>/dev/null || exit 0; "
173	        f"{detach}bash {launcher} < /dev/null > {out_file} 2>&1 &",
174	        user=user,
175	        env=env,
176	        timeout=30,
177	        check=True,
178	        idempotent=True,
179	    )
180	    exit_code = await _await_done_marker(sb, done_file, user=user, time_budget_sec=time_budget_sec)
181	    if exit_code == 0 and not want_output:
182	        return exit_code, ""
183	    if want_output:
184	        return exit_code, await sb.read_file(out_file, user=user)
185	    _, tail, _ = await sb.exec(f"tail -c 512 {out_file} 2>/dev/null", user=user, timeout=15, check=False)
186	    return exit_code, tail or ""

275	        name = type(e).__name__

285	    async def _rpc_retry(self, op_name: str, coro_factory, *, idempotent: bool = True):
286	        """Run coro_factory() with retries for transient E2B RPC failures.
287	
288	        :param idempotent: When False, a transient failure is re-raised instead
289	            of retried: re-running a non-idempotent op (e.g. a process-spawning
290	            exec) after a severed response could double-execute it. Idempotent
291	            ops (the default: create / read_file / write_file / short read-only
292	            execs) retry as before.
293	        """
294	        last_err = None
295	        for attempt in range(self.rpc_retries):
296	            try:
297	                return await coro_factory()
298	            except Exception as e:
299	                if not self._is_transient_rpc_error(e):
300	                    raise
301	                if not idempotent:
302	                    raise
303	                last_err = e
304	                if attempt + 1 < self.rpc_retries:
305	                    await self._reset_conn_pool()
306	                    ceiling = min(self.rpc_backoff_cap_sec, self.rpc_backoff_base_sec * (2**attempt))
307	                    backoff = random.uniform(0.0, ceiling)
308	                    logger.debug(
309	                        "[agent.sandbox] %s transient %s, retry %d/%d in %.1fs: %s",
310	                        op_name,
311	                        type(e).__name__,
312	                        attempt + 1,
313	                        self.rpc_retries,
314	                        backoff,
315	                        str(e)[:120],
316	                    )
317	                    await asyncio.sleep(backoff)
318	        assert last_err is not None
319	        raise last_err

322	async def _apply_diff(ev: Sandbox, workdir: str, diff_text: str) -> bool:
323	    if not diff_text.strip():
324	        return True
325	    await ev.write_file(_PATCH, diff_text, user="agent")
326	    # First-success-wins ladder collapsed into one exec (one sandbox round-trip).
327	    ladder = " || ".join(

329	        for cmd in (
330	            f"git apply --3way --whitespace=nowarn {_PATCH}",
331	            f"git apply --whitespace=nowarn {_PATCH}",
332	            f"patch -p1 --no-backup-if-mismatch < {_PATCH}",
333	        )
334	    )
335	    ec, _, _ = await ev.exec(f"cd {workdir} && ({ladder})", user="agent", check=False, timeout=120)

from a prompt (str or chat-message list).\"\"\"\n    if isinstance(prompt, str):\n        return prompt\n    if isinstance(prompt, list):\n        for m in prompt:\n            if isinstance(m, dict) and m.get(\"role\") == \"user\":\n                return flatten_content(m.get(\"content\"))\n    return \"\"\n\n\ndef evaluability_check(md: dict) -> str | None:\n    if md.get(\"protocol\") == PROTOCOL_SWEBENCH:\n        return _evaluability_check_swebench(md)\n    return \"protocol_row_mismatch:looks_swebench\" if md.get(\"looks_swebench\") else None\n\n\ndef _evaluability_check_swebench(md: dict) -> str | None:\n    if _SWEBENCH_IMPORT_ERROR is not None:\n        return f\"swebench_import_failed:{type(_SWEBENCH_IMPORT_ERROR).__name__}\"\n    inst = md.get(\"grading\", {}).get(\"sweb_instance\") or {}\n    if not inst.get(\"repo\"):\n        return \"missing_repo\"\n    if not inst.get(\"base_commit\"):\n        return \"missing_base_commit\"\n    if not (inst.get(\"test_patch\") or \"\").strip():\n        return \"missing_test_patch\"\n    try:\n        _ = _build_test_spec(inst).eval_script  # surfaces per-repo construction errors here, not later\n    except Exception as e:  # KeyError on unknown repo/version, etc.\n        return f\"make_test_spec_failed:{type(e).__name__}\"\n    return None\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Workspace prep (agent sandbox, before harness.run)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nasync def _open_traversal(sb: Sandbox, workdir: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Open directory traversal for the agent user when the workspace lives\n    under a 700-mode home (e.g. /root/.openclaw/workspace): the agent's execs\n    and file writes cannot reach the workspace otherwise.\"\"\"\n    parts = Path(workdir).parts\n    dirs = []\n    cur = \"\"\n    for p in parts[1:-1]:  # every ancestor except the workspace itself\n        cur = f\"{cur}/{p}\"\n        dirs.append(cur)\n    if dirs:\n        await sb.exec(\"chmod o+x \" + \" \".join(dirs), user=\"root\", timeout=60, check=False)\n\n\nasync def prepare_workspace(sb: Sandbox, workdir: str, md: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Prep the agent sandbox, then drop PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md.\n\n    Assumes the agent user already owns ``workdir`` (the harness's ``run()`` calls\n    ``ensure_agent_user``; the orchestrator runs this before ``run()`` and the\n    agent user is created lazily there). To stay independent of call order we\n    create the agent user here too -- it is idempotent.\n    \"\"\"\n    await _open_traversal(sb, workdir)\n    await agent_sandbox.ensure_agent_user(sb, workdir)\n    if md.get(\"protocol\") == PROTOCOL_SCALESWE:\n        grading = md.get(\"grading\") or {}\n        swepro = grading.get(\"swepro\")\n        if swepro:\n            await apply_before_repo_set_cmd(sb, workdir, swepro)\n        pre_commands = grading.get(\"pre_commands\")\n        if pre_commands:\n            await apply_pre_commands(sb, workdir, pre_commands)\n        # task-instance input files (the workspace resources the prompt\n        # refers to); withheld checker files stay out until verify time\n        for f in grading.get(\"task_files\") or []:\n            await sb.write_file(f\"{workdir}/{f['file_path']}\", f[\"content\"], user=\"agent\")\n    await sb.write_file(\n        f\"{workdir}/PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md\",\n        md.get(\"problem_statement\") or \"\",\n        user=\"agent\",\n    )\n\n\nasync def apply_before_repo_set_cmd(sb: Sandbox, workdir: str, swepro: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Run swepro['before_repo_set_cmd'] in the sandbox if present (no-op if not).\"\"\"\n    before = swepro.get(\"before_repo_set_cmd\")\n    if not before:\n        return\n    payload = f\"set -e\\ncd {workdir}\\n{before}\\n\"\n    await sb.exec(\n        \"mkdir -p /workspace/swepro_setup && chown agent:agent /workspace/swepro_setup\", user=\"root\", check=True\n    )\n    await sb.write_file(\"/workspace/swepro_setup/before.sh\", payload, user=\"agent\")\n    await sb.exec(\"bash /workspace/swepro_setup/before.sh\", user=\"agent\", check=False, timeout=600)\n\n\nasync def apply_pre_commands(sb: Sandbox, workdir: str, pre: list[str] | str) -> None:\n    # Public: also called for the work sandbox to keep its baseline aligned with\n    # eval (sweb-style pre_commands typically `git checkout <base_sha> -f`, so\n    # skipping in the work sandbox makes the model's diff context mismatch the\n    # eval base -> 100% apply failure).\n    if isinstance(pre, str):\n        body = pre.replace(\"\\\\n\", \"\\n\")\n    else:\n        body = \"\\n\".join(c for c in (pre or []) if c)\n    await sb.write_file(_PRE, \"set -e\\n\" + body, user=\"agent\")\n    await sb.exec(f\"chmod 755 {_PRE} && cd {workdir} && bash {_PRE}\", user=\"agent\", check=False, timeout=600)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Diff capture (agent sandbox, after harness.run)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nasync def git_diff(sb: Sandbox, workdir: str) -> str:\n    cmd = f\"cd {workdir} && git add -N . && git diff -- . ':(exclude)PROBLEM_STATEMENT.md' ':(exclude).harness/'\"\n    _, out, _ = await sb.exec(cmd, user=\"agent\", timeout=120)\n    return out\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Eval dispatch (fresh sandbox, apply diff, run dataset tests)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nasync def run_evaluation(md: dict, *, diff_text: str, timeout_sec: int) -> EvalResult:\n    \"\"\"Uniform entry point: dispatch to the protocol's grader.\n\n    No-test-cheating guarantee (both grading protocols): the eval sandbox is built from\n    the same image but starts CLEAN, so only the model-produced diff affects\n    reward.\"\"\"\n    if md.get(\"protocol\") == PROTOCOL_SWEBENCH:\n        return await _grade_swebench(md, diff_text, timeout_sec)\n    return await _grade_scaleswe(md, diff_text, timeout_sec)\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# scaleswe grader\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\nasync def _grade_scaleswe(md: dict, diff_text: str, timeout_sec: int) -> EvalResult:\n    \"\"\"Three mutually-exclusive grading paths, in priority order: swepro test\n    harness, a shell ``eval_cmd``, or a self-contained ``f2p_script`` pytest\n    file. All resolve to \"exit 0 == solved\", reward is 1.0 iff solved.\"\"\"\n    image = md[\"image\"]\n    workdir = md[\"workdir\"]\n    grading = md.get(\"grading\") or {}\n    swepro = grading.get(\"swepro\")\n    eval_cmd = grading.get(\"eval_cmd\")\n    f2p_script = grading.get(\"f2p_script\")\n    pre_commands = grading.get(\"pre_commands\")\n\n    if not (swepro or eval_cmd or f2p_script):\n        logger.warning(\"[swe.scaleswe] no swepro/eval_cmd/f2p_script; reward=0\")\n        return EvalResult(0.0, True)\n\n    async with E2BSandbox(image) as ev:\n        await agent_sandbox.ensure_agent_user(ev, workdir)\n        if swepro:\n            await _setup_swepro_assets(ev, swepro)\n            await apply_before_repo_set_cmd(ev, workdir, swepro)\n        if pre_commands:\n            await apply_pre_commands(ev, workdir, pre_commands)\n\n        applied = await _apply_diff(ev, workdir, diff_text)\n        if not applied:\n            return EvalResult(0.0, False)\n\n        if swepro:\n            r = await _run_swepro(ev, workdir, swepro, timeout_sec)\n        elif eval_cmd:\n            r = await _run_eval_cmd(ev, workdir, eval_cmd, timeout_sec)\n        else:\n            r = await _run_f2p_script(ev, workdir, f2p_script, timeout_sec)\n        return EvalResult(r, True)\n\n\nasync def _setup_swepro_assets(ev: Sandbox, swepro: dict) -> None:\n    await ev.exec(f\"mkdir -p {_SWEPRO_DIR} && chmod 777 {_SWEPRO_DIR}\", user=\"root\", check=True)\n    for k, dst in [(\"run_script_path\", \"run_script.sh\"), (\"parser_script_path\", \"parser.py\")]:\n        host_p = swepro.get(k)\n        if host_p:\n            await ev.write_file(f\"{_SWEPRO_DIR}/{dst}\", Path(host_p), user=\"root\")\n    await ev.exec(f\"chmod 755 {_SWEPRO_DIR}/* && chown -R agent:agent {_SWEPRO_DIR}\", user=\"root\", check=True)\n\n\nasync def _apply_diff(ev: Sandbox, workdir: str, diff_text: str) -> bool:\n    if not diff_text.strip():\n        return True\n    await ev.write_file(_PATCH, diff_text, user=\"agent\")\n    # First-success-wins ladder collapsed into one exec (one sandbox round-trip).\n    ladder = \" || \".join(\n        f\"({cmd})\"\n        for cmd in (\n            f\"git apply --3way --whitespace=nowarn {_PATCH}\",\n            f\"git apply --whitespace=nowarn {_PATCH}\",\n            f\"patch -p1 --no-backup-if-mismatch < {_PATCH}\",\n        )\n    )\n    ec, _, _ = await ev.exec(f\"cd {workdir} && ({ladder})\", user=\"agent\", check=False, timeout=120)\n    return ec == 0\n\n\nasync def _run_swepro(ev: Sandbox, workdir: str, swepro: dict, timeout: int) -> float:\n    test_arg = \",\".join(swepro.get(\"selected_test_files\") or [])\n    stdout_f = f\"{_SWEPRO_DIR}/stdout.log\"\n    stderr_f = f\"{_SWEPRO_DIR}/stderr.log\"\n    result_f = f\"{_SWEPRO_DIR}/result.json\"\n    await ev.exec(\n        f\"cd {workdir} && bash {_SWEPRO_DIR}/run_script.sh {json.dumps(test_arg)} > {stdout_f} 2> {stderr_f} || true\",\n        user=\"agent\",\n        check=False,\n        timeout=timeout,\n    )\n    await ev.exec(\n        f\"python3 {_SWEPRO_DIR}/parser.py {stdout_f} {stderr_f} {result_f}\",\n        user=\"agent\",\n        check=False,\n        timeout=120,\n    )\n    raw = await ev.read_file(result_f, user=\"agent\")\n    parsed = json.loads(raw) if raw else {\"tests\": []}\n    passed = {t[\"name\"] for t in parsed.get(\"tests\", []) if t.get(\"status\") == \"PASSED\"}\n    required = set(swepro.get(\"fail_to_pass\") or []) | set(swepro.get(\"pass_to_pass\") or [])\n    solved = bool(required) and required.issubset(passed)\n    return 1.0 if solved else 0.0\n\n\nasync def _run_eval_cmd(ev: Sandbox, workdir: str, cmd: str, timeout: int) -> float:\n    ec, _, _ = await ev.exec(f\"cd {workdir} && {cmd}\", user=\"agent\", check=False, timeout=timeout)\n    return 1.0 if ec == 0 else 0.0\n\n\nasync def _run_f2p_script(ev: and\n    # let python's exit code carry the pass/fail signal.\n    await ev.write_file(_F2P, script, user=\"agent\")\n    ec, _, _ = await ev.exec(f\"cd {workdir} && python {_F2P}\", user=\"agent\", The `patch --fuzz` tier rescues diffs `git apply` rejects.\n_GIT_APPLY_CMDS = (\n    \"git apply --verbose\",\n    \"git apply --verbose --reject\",\n    \"patch --batch --fuzz=5 -p1 -i\",\n)\n\n\nasync def _apply_model_patch(ev: Sandbox, workdir: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Apply /tmp/patch.diff via the GIT_APPLY_CMDS ladder; True if applied\n    (or empty). Empty patch is a no-op success -- eval then scores it 0 on its\n    own (no source change -> tests still fail).\"\"\"\n    ladder = \" || \".join(f\"{cmd} /tmp/patch.diff\" for cmd in _GIT_APPLY_CMDS)\n    cmd = (\n        f\"cd {workdir} && git config --global --add safe.directory {workdir} \"\n        f\"&& if [ -s /tmp/patch.diff ]; then {ladder}; fi\"\n    )\n    ec, _, _ = await ev.exec(cmd, user=\"root\", check=False, timeout=120)\n    return ec == 0\n\n\ndef _build_test_spec(inst: dict):\n    \"\"\"make_test_spec(inst). Shared by evaluability_check and the grader; may\n    raise (KeyError on unknown repo/version).\"\"\"\n    return make_test_spec(inst)  # type: ignore[misc]\n\n\ndef _eval_report_from_log(ts, instance_id: str, diff_text: str, log: str) -> dict:\n    \"\"\"Run swebench's get_eval_report against the captured test log. It reads\n    from a file path, so write the log to a tempfile, parse, and clean up.\"\"\"\n    tmp = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(mode=\"w\", suffix=\".log\", delete=False)\n    try:\n        tmp.write(log)\n        tmp.flush()\n        tmp.close()\n        prediction = {\n            \"instance_id\": instance_id,\n            \"model_patch\": diff_text or \"\",\n            \"model_name_or_path\": \"swe\",\n        }\n        return get_eval_report(  # type: ignore[misc]\n            test_spec=ts,\n            prediction=prediction,\n            test_log_path=tmp.name,\n            include_tests_status=True,\n        )\n    finally:\n        try:\n            os.unlink(tmp.name)\n        except OSError:\n            pass\n\n\ndef _ratio(d: dict) -> tuple[int, int]:\n    \"\"\"(passed, total) from a {success: [...], failure: [...]} bucket.\"\"\"\n    passed, failed = d.get(\"success\", []), d.get(\"failure\", [])\n    return len(passed), len(passed) + len(failed)\n\n\ndef _log_swebench_result(instance_id: str, exit_code, info: dict, log: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit the per-instance grading outcome with test-bucket ratios; on a\n    non-resolved row that parsed NO test lines, surface the log tail so failures\n    (missing pytest plugin, conda not activated, ...) can be diagnosed.\"\"\"\n    if info.get(\"resolved\"):\n        logger.info(\"[swe.swebench] %s: reward=1 exit_code=%s\", instance_id, exit_code)\n        return\n    ts_status = info.get(\"tests_status\") or {}\n    f2p_pass, f2p_total = _ratio(ts_status.get(\"FAIL_TO_PASS\", {}))\n    p2p_pass, p2p_total = _ratio(ts_status.get(\"PASS_TO_PASS\", {}))\n    nothing_parsed = not (f2p_total or p2p_total)\n    tail = log[-800:] if nothing_parsed else \"\"\n    logger.info(\n        \"[swe.swebench] %s: reward=0 exit_code=%s patch_applied=%s F2P=(%d/%d) P2P=(%d/%d)%s\",\n        instance_id,\n        exit_code,\n        bool(info.get(\"patch_successfully_applied\")),\n        f2p_pass,\n        f2p_total,\n        p2p_pass,\n        p2p_total,\n        f\" tail={tail!r}\" if tail else \"\",\n    )\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Local same-sandbox verify chain (team fork)\n#\n# Against the local sandbox backend the whole episode lives in one sandbox\n# instance: the agent works there, and at the end the hidden tests are uploaded\n# into the SAME instance and graded there (no fresh eval sandbox). The chain is\n# two layers, mirroring the production conversion pipeline:\n#\n#   tests/test.sh   (conversion wrapper)  -> reward/reward.sh  (checker)\n#   wrapper: checker rc!=0  =>  reward.txt = 0.0, wrapper exits 0\n#           : checker rc==0  =>  reward.txt = checker stdout (the score)\n#\n# and run_local_evaluation below folds any verify-side failure (instance\n# unreachable, upload/readback failure, unparseable score) into a legal 0.0 as\n# well, so the rollout loop always sees a completed, scored episode.\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n_LOCAL_VERIFY_WRAPPER = \"\"\"#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Conversion wrapper: run the checker and normalize its outcome into the\n# score file. A non-zero checker status, or a score the checker failed to\n# emit in a parseable form, maps to 0.0; the wrapper itself always exits 0\n# so the outer loop treats the episode as scored.\ncd \"$(dirname \"$0\")/..\"\nmkdir -p verify\nbash reward/reward.sh > verify/reward.raw 2> verify/checker.err\nrc=$?\nscore=$(python3 - <<'PYEOF'\nimport json, os, re\nraw = \"\"\nif os.path.exists(\"verify/reward.raw\"):\n    raw = open(\"verify/reward.raw\", encoding=\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").read()\nscore = None\ntry:\n    obj = json.loads(raw)\n    if isinstance(obj, dict):\n        vals = [v for v in obj.values() if isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool)]\n        if vals:\n            score = sum(vals) / len(vals)", "numLines": 500, "startLine": 1, "totalLines": 633}}
